trust_decision.summary: Which option values configure the pool and its spawned workers (execArgv, env, argv, loadBalancer, resourceLimits, workerData, per-call run/close options) is decided by property reads on ordinary objects, so keys the caller never set resolve through Object.prototype; the ThreadPool constructor re-spreads the caller's options over defaults into an ordinary object, and that object feeds new Worker(...) and the balancer.

landing_point.why: The summary names ThreadPool.options; this line builds it by spreading kDefaultOptions and the caller's options into a plain object, and the gadget keys execArgv/env/loadBalancer are read from it at src/index.ts:209 and src/index.ts:237-239.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Build the Worker options bag with a defaults spread (e.g. { ...kDefaultWorkerOptions, ...workerOpts }) so an extra key such as stdout/stderr or name is read inherited
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: WorkerInfo is a separate layer that receives a plain worker options object; a maintainer adding a new worker option would naturally spread defaults here, away from the fixed ThreadPool merge

O8b_injection_room.sibling: LeastBusyBalancer option bag read by plain destructuring; adding optional balancer options (for example a scoring hook) merged from pool options would reintroduce an inherited function call
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The balancer is a separate module that takes its own opts object; extending it with optional callbacks is a plausible feature

O8b_injection_room.sibling: runTask destructures filename/name/signal/transferList from its options; a second internal caller (for example a planted runMany/batch API) passing caller options straight through would bypass the run() copy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: runTask is the shared lower-level path behind run(); a new public helper calling it directly is plausible and sits behind the fixed copy
